title: List Price Movement and the Reviewed Escalation Increase, Contract Pricing Agreement Contract Items
content:
## List price movement and the reviewed escalation increase — Contract Pricing Agreement

When an annual escalation of a Contract Pricing Agreement contract item is reviewed on a pending price claim, the reviewed escalation increase is measured from the item's new-item line to its escalation line, and Corbett's list price on those two lines decides how:

| List price between the two lines | Reviewed escalation increase |
|---|---|
| Rose, but by less than the supplier cost rose | The percentage rise in list price |
| Did not rise, while the supplier cost did | 0 |
| Every other case | The supplier cost increase (the percentage increase in supplier cost between the two lines) |

Percentage rises are the later figure divided by the earlier figure, less one, expressed in percent.

**Cases (hypothetical figures).**
- Supplier cost up 6 percent, list price up 3 percent: increase 3 percent.
- Supplier cost up 6 percent, list price unchanged or lower: increase 0.
- Supplier cost up 6 percent, list price up 8 percent: increase 6 percent.
- Supplier cost down 2 percent, list price down 1 percent: neither of the first two rows applies, so the increase is the supplier cost increase, less than 0.
